messages:
mira: quick sync — experimenting with a "microbeam warmup" variant for speculative decode on llama3-70b-4bit. idea: do a short beam on the first ~16 tokens, keep top-k kv snapshots, then continue sampling off those snapshots. goal is to reduce distributional shift when switching from warmup -> stochastic sampling and cut tail latency. curious if ppl want to try on the 2k eval set this week.
sam: sounds neat. rough perf overhead?
mira: local devbox numbers (4x A100p, 70b q4): baseline top-p sampling p50 token latency ~70ms. microbeam warmup (beam=4, warmup_len=16, cache_top_k=2) -> warmup adds ~480ms extra start latency but amortized per-token latency falls to ~60ms and 99p tail drops ~25%. throughput mixed (depends on request length).
kai: can you paste the config you ran?
mira: sure:
```json
{
  "model":"llama3-70b-q4_0",
  "microbeam":{
    "beam":4,
    "warmup_len":16,
    "cache_top_k":2,
    "early_prune":0.6
  },
  "sampling":{
    "top_p":0.92,
    "temp":0.8
  }
}
```

olivia: eval plan? how are we measuring quality impact vs baseline sampling?
mira: for quick check: automatic metrics (exact-match for QA pairs, BLEU + chrF on longform where relevant), + n=200 human spot-check on safety/fluency. also track KL between microbeam-conditioned logits and baseline logits at token positions 17-32 (post-warmup).
kai: important to fix RNG seeds and control quantization nondeterminism. for quantized models we saw small nondet from kernel ordering. recommend 20 fixed seeds and aggregate. also include 8-bit run as control.

sam: any quality regressions so far?
mira: small drop on openbookqa EM: -0.6 pts (stat sig borderline), but longform chrF improved slightly (~+0.4). hypothesis: warmup reduces weird early divergence that causes sampling to chase low-prob tails.

olivia: what about fail cases? any hallucination mode change?
mira: spotted a case where warmup reinforced a wrong early token in beam and kept it — early_prune helped but needs tuning. we also saw a prompt family (instruction style with long preface) where warmup length 16 is too short; setting warmup_len adaptive to prefix length seems promising.

bench-bot: queued job 7890: run microbeam-warmup sweep (beam=[2,4,8], warmup_len=[8,16,32], cache_top_k=[1,2]) on eval-2k. ETA ~3h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

kai: for eval harness: please output per-prompt logits diff and per-token delta-likelihood. also log nvprof counters for KB cache hits if possible.

mira: will do. my suggested acceptance criteria before we roll to canary:
- no >1.0pt drop on primary QA EM metric across eval-2k
- 95p tail latency improvement >=15%
- human fluency regressions <=3%

sam: also add cost model: warmup cost vs token savings. rough back-of-envelope for our traffic mix (avg len 80): warmup pays off if warmup_len * added_warmup_cost_per_token < token_savings_post_warmup * per-token-cost. can compute from bench outputs.

olivia: volunteers to triage regressions? I can take the openbookqa diffs and do n=50 manual labeling.
mira: thanks — assigning openbookqa -> olivia, I'll take longform tests + kernel nondet investigation. kai can you keep an eye on the sweep logs and nv counters?
kai: on it.

mira: if bench results look promising I'll stage a canary in dedicated pool (low qps) next week. tagging: @sam @kai @olivia.

sam: +1.

mira: cool — will post results here when bench-bot finishes (job 7890).
